title: Artin's affine support estimate for the direct image at finite coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Use the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of finite type [pqf-def-affine-morphism] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $Rf_*$ be the right derived functor of the module direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on $D^+(-_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Let $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and satisfy the support condition: for every $i$ the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) of $\mathcal H^{-i}L$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] has dimension at most $i$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$, as in [def-per-support-condition] read at finite coefficients. Then $Rf_*L$ is bounded with constructible cohomology sheaves and satisfies the support condition.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1 (Artin's estimate: Rf_* of an affine morphism preserves pD^{<=0})

proof.text: For $i<0$ the closed support of $\mathcal H^{-i}L$ has dimension $<0$, so it is empty and $\mathcal H^{-i}L=0$. As $L$ is bounded below, it has only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves $F_i=\mathcal H^{-i}L$, $0\le i\le N$, each constructible with closed support $Z_i$ of dimension at most $i$.

source.place: 2.1.2: the support condition bounds the degrees

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $q\ge0$. A point $x$ with $(F_i)_{\bar x}\ne0$ lies in $Z_i$, so $\overline{\{x\}}\subset Z_i$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)=\dim\overline{\{x\}}\le i$ [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg]: the support of $F_i$ in the sense of [def-kun-support] lies in $E_i(X)$. Cohomology of $\Lambda$-module sheaves agrees with that of the underlying abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget], which are torsion, so [lem-kun-affine-direct-image-support-bound] shows that every point $y$ with $(R^qf_*F_i)_{\bar y}\ne0$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)\le i-q$. The sheaf $R^qf_*F_i$ is constructible [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], so its closed support is the finite union of the closures of the generic points of its components, which have nonzero stalks (as in Step 1 of [lem-per-finite-compact-support-fibre-support-bound]); each has dimension $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)\le i-q$ by [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg]. Thus the closed support of $R^qf_*F_i$ has dimension at most $i-q$.

source.place: Tag 0F0X (Lemma 59.95.8): the support of R^q f_* F lies in E_{a-q}(Y)

proof.text: Hence $\mathcal H^{j}(Rf_*(F_i[i]))=R^{i+j}f_*F_i$ has closed support of dimension at most $-j$ and vanishes for $i+j<0$: $Rf_*(F_i[i])$ satisfies the support condition. The truncation triangles of the standard t-structure [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] build $L$ from the finitely many $F_i[i]$; $Rf_*$ is triangulated, and the support condition is closed under extensions (the middle cohomology sheaf of a triangle vanishes where both outer ones vanish). So $Rf_*L$ satisfies the support condition. It is bounded with constructible cohomology by [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility].
